status: Open collection questions with bounded progress from worked cases and military-domain research; no outreach sent

questions.question: What authority is actually delegated for a named autonomous function?
questions.request: Named system's final operating rule and acceptance record specifying authorization, supervision, intervention, override and responsibility; do not substitute intent specifications.
questions.wouldChange: Distinguish policy commitments from implemented authority boundaries.
questions.alternativeExplanation: Human-control language may coexist with extensive task automation; it does not specify continuous human input.

progress.finding: Earlier cases identify remote control, task entry and requested modes. CH-4’s civilian customer reports ground-station takeoff/return commands; Zhuhai Yun’s operating institute supplies crew and survey managers. These add system-specific human roles, without a universal PLA authority rule or tested override. A reported Air Force transport-scheduling trial shifts people toward exception review; its observed simulation does not establish an adopted authority rule. Final civil conditions for the Wing Loong-2 meteorological model specify operator workload, automatic-flight interruption and control handover. These are requirements, without original test results or a demonstrated PLA override.

questions.question: Which external dependencies are present in the customer's actual configuration?
questions.request: Purchased configuration and firmware inventory, locked environment for one result, and a migration record with engineering time, retraining, regressions and qualification.
questions.wouldChange: Identify a concrete dependency and switching burden without treating nationality as a complete stack description.
questions.alternativeExplanation: A public research repository may not be the shipping controller; an optional processor is not installed in every model.

progress.finding: Six official Unitree repositories inspected at pinned commits; dependencies, binary boundaries and alternative interfaces/simulators identified. Shipping configuration and switching cost remain unverified. Named civilian software and a commercial sensor are documented in military-university research. Exact historical software commits and operating military configurations remain unknown. Shenzhen’s 2026 plan calls for ROS toolkit migration; completed substitutions and switching costs are not established.

questions.question: How much human work remains per accepted task?
questions.request: Matched accepted-task, intervention and person-hour logs; separate training, commissioning, live control, recovery, ground support and fallback.
questions.wouldChange: Calculate bounded workflow economics and characterize the actual division of work.
questions.alternativeExplanation: Labor may move to integration or recovery rather than disappear; data-collection teleoperation does not imply live teleoperation.

progress.finding: Concrete jobs now include military aircraft assembly/maintenance/test work, civilian ground-station commands and research-vessel crew/operations. Retained work is observable; matched task, person-hour, intervention and cost records remain absent. EACON reports a named quarry with 23 autonomous trucks and two on-site staff per shift, but off-site and customer work remain outside that count. A military rental notice explicitly buys aircraft plus pilots.

questions.question: Does performance survive the stated operating envelope?
questions.request: Civilian field results with version, load/posture, temperature, duration, sensor/compute configuration, support infrastructure, failures and accepted outputs.
questions.wouldChange: Separate laboratory or peak capability from repeatable use under customer conditions.
questions.alternativeExplanation: A favorable demonstration may omit cooling, charging, difficult inputs or recovery time.

progress.finding: Cooling support and configuration distinctions expose why autonomy performance depends on the surrounding system. No matched independent field envelope established. EACON reports an initial quarry fleet operating for more than 23 months; this is positive deployment-history evidence without a matched independent operating-envelope evaluation.

questions.question: Who creates and owns the integration that makes the workflow useful?
questions.request: Named integrator/customer scope of work, software version, acceptance criteria and support contract; compare engineering hours across repeat deployments.
questions.wouldChange: Attribute value and recurring work across OEM, integrator, software provider and customer.
questions.alternativeExplanation: A successful deployment may depend on extensive site-specific engineering rather than a general-purpose model.

progress.finding: The naval warehouse collaboration and Jingpin software progress are supplemented by Zhuhai Yun’s separately named owner, designer, builder, supplier and operating institute. Joint-laboratory governance identifies institutional bridges; neither supplies repeat-deployment engineering costs or complete IP ownership. Baishihu reports customer-led interoperability across three vendors, and a PLA transport trial reports internal software development. Retained integration work does not identify which organization captures its value. Consys filings distinguish a competed ground-computing product from a separate commission, with later category-level supply reporting. They do not disclose integration margins or identify a common software implementation.

questions.question: What specific artifact or capability crossed the civil–military boundary?
questions.request: Versioned evidence connecting the documented research artifacts to an integrated military product; identify distribution or contracting mechanism, acceptance and any common civil/military implementation. Keep institutional participation and research use separate from direct supply.
questions.wouldChange: Promote a technical-relevance hypothesis into a bounded relationship; operating capability still requires separate evidence.
questions.alternativeExplanation: Similar technologies or institutions may have no documented transfer relationship.

progress.finding: Five Eight claims a military robot-wolf platform contribution; warehouse reporting identifies civilian collaboration. Haiyi’s disclosed license/IP sale establishes a bounded research-to-commercial mechanism, with no military destination established. NUDT’s private-firm exhibition establishes contact only. Exact shared shipping military/civilian software or accepted transferred autonomy remains unresolved. A provisional military public-health package lists DJI/XAG models through a trading supplier: concrete commercial-product procurement evidence, with acceptance and autonomy functions unverified. Research-stage software evaluation and commercial-component use are now explicit. Those links establish neither direct vendor military contracts nor accepted fielded software; the separate Consys procurement case does not prove civilian technology origin.

questions.question: Which claims are backed by a formal requirement and which by actual testing?
questions.request: Operator-specific approved program/permissions or final procurement specification, plus separate configuration-specific test and acceptance records.
questions.wouldChange: Distinguish an authoritative rule, a draft, a participant list and tested conformity.
questions.alternativeExplanation: A standard's existence or a company's drafting participation does not establish conformity.

progress.finding: Prior training-standard and procurement-intent records are joined by CH-4 aircraft-specific qualification reporting, Zhuhai Yun’s reported classification/trials, and a UAV provisional selection with a failed package. Original model-specific acceptance records remain missing; the equipment-research regulation was reviewed only through its promulgation announcement. Issuer recognition policies and a glider shipment-to-recognition example distinguish accepted business from shipping and routine operation; they are not system-specific autonomy acceptance tests. Effective civil model-specific conditions, an issuer conformity-progress statement, military-export approval reporting and ground-equipment qualification reporting now have separate records. No original PLA function-specific acceptance result was obtained.

questions.question: Do newer learned policies reduce adaptation and recovery work at a new site?
questions.request: Held-out task/site evaluation with adaptation data, training time, human recovery, compute configuration and pre/post release comparison.
questions.wouldChange: Connect model progress to deployment effort and accepted output.
questions.alternativeExplanation: A benchmark gain can depend on extra demonstrations, a different embodiment or compute unavailable in the deployed configuration.

progress.finding: Multiple development routes are documented, but no matched evidence of reduced adaptation or recovery work was obtained.
